facts.raw_span: progressive, multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques localized to the left shin for more than 10 years
milia and a few erosions with partially detached epidermis were identified
no abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
no extracutaneous involvement was observed
Multiple pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques on the left shin
Close-up examination revealed erosion with partially detached epidermis and multiple milia
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Histopathologic examination revealed several milia in the superficial dermis
Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant, c.6832G>T, p.Gly2278Trp, in COL7A1 (NM_000094)
Sanger sequencing confirmed cosegregation of this variant

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including progressive itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques, milia, and erosions with partially detached epidermis, along with the histopathologic examination revealing dermoepidermal separation and milia in the superficial dermis, are consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa, a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the COL7A1 gene, as confirmed by whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing.

The patient's symptoms, including pruritic erythematous to violaceous lichenified papules and plaques, and the presence of milia and erosions, could also be consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita, an autoimmune disorder that can present with similar skin lesions.

rationales.F01: The presence of progressive, multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques is more typical of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F02: Milia and erosions are more commonly seen in Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F07: Dermoepidermal separation is a hallmark of Epidermolysis Bullosa, but the specific type is more consistent with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa given the other findings.
rationales.F09: The novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 is highly suggestive of Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
rationales.F10: Cosegregation of the variant with the disease phenotype further supports Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
